title: Emission chronometer ledger and KV-economics attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a low-overhead token emission chronometer and ledger that attributes per-token latency and cost deltas to KV cache behavior and batching. This ticket covers: (1) span conventions and trace hooks to capture per-emission microtimings, (2) a minimal sidecar telemetry envelope emitted to Kafka for aggregation, (3) ClickHouse schema and rollup jobs for day-level billing reconciliation, and (4) Grafana dashboards + alerts for latency/cost regressions. The output will feed Redwood Console's per-route cost breakdown and the Optimize recommendations pipeline. We will prioritize backwards-compatible trace/span names and avoid adding high-cardinality labels beyond "model", "route", "cache_hit", and "segment_index". Sampling: 1% full-trace captures (detailed spans + token timings) + 100% lightweight metrics (counter/gauge probes) for each request.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument runtime to emit per-emission microtimings (microseconds) with span IDs and request IDs
Kafka topic telemetry.tokens.v1 receives envelope for both sampled and lightweight captures
ClickHouse table tokens_attribution_v1 stores daily aggregates and supports query patterns used by billing reconciliation and SLO dashboards
Grafana dashboard shows per-route token latency breakdown and a KV-cache delta chart (p50/p95/p99)
Automated alert when average per-token latency delta exceeds 20% for 15 minutes on any production route
telemetry_schema: fields: request_id, trace_id, span_id, model, route, host_pool, sequence_len, segment_index
batch_id: optional string for batched requests
token_cost_estimate_usd: computed token-level cost based on kernel time and gpu_rate
implementation_notes: Trace hooks: add a thin hook in the serving runtime to start a child span per emission subsequence before KV lookup and end after decode
Prefer OpenTelemetry semantic attributes; keep custom attributes limited to avoid cardinality explosions
Lightweight capture will emit a single aggregated envelope per request for high-volume routes and include aggregated per-token histograms
Full-trace capture stores per-token microtimings and a cache_hit boolean for delta analysis; subject to sampling policy
Emit to Kafka topic telemetry.tokens.v1; schema evolution via version header in envelope
ClickHouse schema uses MergeTree with daily partitioning and pre-aggregated rollups for p50/p95/p99 per route+model
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: high-cardinality attributes increase storage and query cost. Mitigation: only include model, route, host_pool, and segment_index; map rare routes to 'other' during ingest
Risk: tracing overhead on hot paths. Mitigation: keep hot-path fast-path for lightweight capture; guard detailed spans behind sampling and a runtime flag
Risk: cost-estimate divergence vs billing. Mitigation: reconcile estimates with actual infra billing in a reconciliation job and surface correction factors

2026-03-11 - Ravi: ClickHouse DDL draft uploaded. Proposed table tokens_attribution_v1 with columns (day, route, model, cache_hit, segment_index, count, p50_us, p95_us, p99_us, total_cost_usd). Will iterate.
2026-03-12 - Marta: Dashboard wireframe attached in Figma and linked in PR. Need final labels and colours for cache_hit vs miss comparison widget.
2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Integrated feedback. Next: run 2-week shadow run on staging with 100% lightweight capture and 0.5% full-trace sampling, validate aggregation jobs and dashboard queries.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow): 2026-03-15 -> 2026-03-29 staging shadow run with lightweight capture enabled, 0.5% full-trace sampling
Phase 1 (gradual prod): 2026-03-30 enable lightweight capture on 10% prod traffic; 0.5% full-trace sampling
Phase 2 (expand): after 7 days of stable metrics, ramp lightweight capture to 100% and keep full-trace at 1%
Rollback criteria: sustained >1% increase in p99 tail on any critical route for 30 minutes; any unhandled memory pressure in runtime sidecar
notes_for_reviews: When reviewing runtime PR pay attention to allocation patterns inside the chronometer path to avoid extra heap churn
Ingest reviewers: validate schema regression tests and the ability to map legacy telemetry to v1 envelopes
Analytics reviewers: confirm ClickHouse rollups answer queries used by Console without expensive group-bys at runtime
